ing: dried salted yogurt balls; or 1.5 cups plain Greek yogurt plus 1 tsp salt
st: Crumble the qurut into a bowl, pour over [[1 cup]] hot water and mash to a creamy sauce. If using yogurt, whisk it with the salt and a splash of water.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onions until golden and soft.
Warm the flatbread in the oven or a dry pan, then tear into pieces.
Spread the bread on a large platter.
Spoon the qurut sauce over the bread so it soaks in.
Top with the golden onions and some of their oil.
Arrange the tomatoes and cucumber on top and scatter with herbs.
Serve right away, eating from the shared platter.
Soak the rinsed rice in warm salted water while you cook the meat.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat until shimmering. Brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onions and cook until deep golden.
Add the carrots, [[1 tbsp]] cumin seeds and [[2 tsp]] salt, and cook until the carrots soften.
Pour in [[1 cup]] boiling water, add the chickpeas, cover and simmer until the lamb is tender. This is the zirvak.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the meat. Do not stir.
Pour [[2.5 cups]] boiling water gently down the side, nestle in the garlic head, and cook on high until the water is level with the rice.
Make small holes in the rice with a spoon handle, cover tightly, and steam on the lowest heat until the rice is tender. Mix gently and serve.
Mix the flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and water into a firm dough. Knead until smooth and rest, covered.
Mix the lamb, onions, cumin, pepper, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter for the filling. Keep it cold.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll the dough thin on a floured counter and cut into squares about the size of your palm.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Fold into triangles and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Place on the sheet, brush with egg and butter, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake until golden and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Put the lamb in a large pot with [[8 cups]] cold water. Bring to a boil.
Skim off the foam that rises.
Add the onions, [[2 tsp]] salt and pepper. Cover and simmer on low until the lamb is tender.
Add the carrots and chickpeas and simmer.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes and bell pepper.
Cook until all the vegetables are soft.
Taste and adjust salt. Lift out the lamb, pull the meat off the bones and return it to the pot.
Ladle into bowls and top with cilantro.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and water into a stiff dough. Knead until smooth and rest, covered.
Mix the lamb, onions, pumpkin, cumin, pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into squares of about 4 inches.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Bring up the corners and pinch the edges to seal into a closed parcel.
Grease the steamer tiers with oil and arrange the mantu without touching.
Steam over boiling water until the dough is tender and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Brush with melted butter and serve hot, with yogurt or sour cream.
Heat the oil in a large pot over high heat and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the bell peppers, radish and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in [[3 cups]] stock, add [[1.5 tsp]] salt, and simmer covered until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Boil the noodles in salted water until tender, then drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls.
Spoon the hot meat and vegetable sauce over the noodles.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and water and rest until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl, add the yeast mixture and oil, and knead into a soft dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking stone or heavy tray inside.
Divide the dough into four balls. Flatten each into a round, leaving a thicker rim.
Press the center with a fork or a bread stamp to make small holes so it will not puff.
Brush with a little water and sprinkle with sesame and nigella seeds.
Bake each on the hot stone until golden brown. Serve warm.
Slice the onions as thinly as possible and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Squeeze the onions lightly with your hands to soften and remove bitterness, then rinse and drain.
Slice the tomatoes and cucumber into thin rounds.
Arrange the tomatoes, overlapping, on a plate.
Layer the cucumber and onions on top.
Scatter the chili, cilantro and basil over the salad.
Season with the remaining salt and pepper.
Let it sit so the juices mingle, then serve with bread or plov.
